result.question: Why did the four men with leprosy go to the camp of the Arameans?

readings.answer: To have a chance to live
readings.support: So come now, let us go over to the camp of the Arameans. | If they let us live, we will live

readings.answer: Because staying or entering the city meant death
readings.support: we will die there from the famine in the city; but if we sit here, we will also die. | So come now, let us go over to the camp of the Arameans.

assessments.reason: “If they let us live, we will live” shows they went for the chance to live, which is part of the passage’s stated motive even though it omits the certainty of death if they stayed or entered the city.

“We will die there from the famine in the city; but if we sit here, we will also die” explains that other options meant death, which motivated going to the Arameans, though it omits the stated possibility that they might let them live.
